The blur needs to draw over other apps. Best: allow it with Shizuku (turns on the Waaiya Blur accessibility service, so touches still reach the app underneath). Or allow "Display over other apps" in Android settings (touches on a blurred area are then lost).

The blur needs to draw over other apps. Best: start Shizuku (and allow Waaiya in it): the blur then draws its own layer, which taps pass through. Otherwise allow "Display over other apps" in Android settings; a tap on a blurred area then does not reach the app underneath.

You need Wi-Fi and Android 11 or newer. Pairing is done once; after the phone restarts you only repeat step 7.

1. Connect the phone to Wi-Fi.

2. Turn on Developer options: Settings › About phone › Software information › tap “Build number” 7 times. (On other phones: Settings › About phone › Build number.)

3. Open Shizuku. If it asks to show notifications, allow it: the pairing code is typed in a Shizuku notification.

4. In Shizuku, under “Start via Wireless debugging”, tap “Pairing”. On the page that opens, tap “Developer options”, turn on “Wireless debugging” and confirm “Allow”.

5. Tap the words “Wireless debugging” (not the switch), then “Pair device with pairing code”. A 6-digit code appears.

6. Keep that screen open and pull down the notifications. When Shizuku's notification says “Pairing service found”, tap “Enter pairing code” and type the code. Shizuku says pairing succeeded.

7. Go back to Shizuku and tap “Start” under “Start via Wireless debugging”. Wait until it says “Shizuku is running”.

8. Come back to Waaiya and tap “Give permission”, then “Allow”.

After a phone restart Shizuku stops: connect to Wi-Fi, turn “Wireless debugging” back on if it is off, open Shizuku and tap “Start”. No new pairing.
Set up on this phone (no extra app)
With Android\'s own Wireless debugging. You need Wi-Fi (internet is not needed). Pairing is done once.

1. Tap “Start”. Waaiya opens Developer options and shows a notification.

2. If Developer options are off, About phone opens instead: tap “Build number” 7 times (on some phones it is under Software information), come back and tap “Start” again.

3. Turn on “Wireless debugging” and confirm “Allow”.

4. Tap the words “Wireless debugging” (not the switch), then “Pair device with pairing code”. A 6-digit code appears.

5. Keep that screen open. Pull down the notifications, tap “Enter code” in Waaiya's notification and type the code.

6. Waaiya finishes by itself and says “Setup done”. You can then turn Wireless debugging off.
Android 10 cannot do the setup on its own: it needs a computer, directly (below) or to start Shizuku once.
Shizuku also lets touches pass through the screen covers.

The 6-digit code from “Pair device with pairing code”. If Waaiya has not found the pairing screen, add the port shown under “IP address & Port”, for example 123456 37123.

Anyone the app is not sure is a man is covered. Strict leaves about 7 men in 100 uncovered; balanced about 14, relaxed about 16. Each step less strict also leaves about 1 more woman in 100 uncovered.
